notInScope: whether the canonical statement is the informal problem (a reading, F5): F2 tests it on finitely many instances, which is evidence, not proof; the planted statements marked "kernel decides" carry no prediction; the claimant's file is never copied; the claimant's declaration is an axiom: it has no proof to replace, so no defect of its file is planted by rule
success: among the planted statements that reach the check, every certain prediction met (ACCEPTED; NOT ACCEPTED, met only by a refusal by type mismatch; the F2 ⇒ F1 rule), at least one changed or retyped statement refused and one rewording accepted; a statement that does not elaborate is not tested and is counted neither way; every planted defect of the claimant's file caught, F3 and F2 as their rules say
